claim: Reverse transcriptase activity has never been demonstrated before for RNA.
source: A highly evolved RNA polymerase ribozyme was found to also be capable of functioning as a reverse transcriptase, an activity that has never been demonstrated before for RNA.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the existing scientific literature on RNA enzymes.

claim: Reverse transcriptase activity is thought to have been crucial for the transition from RNA to DNA genomes during the early history of life on Earth.
source: This activity is thought to have been crucial for the transition from RNA to DNA genomes during the early history of life on Earth, when it similarly could have arisen as a secondary function of an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the historical role of reverse transcriptase in early life, based on inference from current findings.

claim: Reverse transcriptase activity could have arisen as a secondary function of an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase during early life on Earth.

claim: The reverse transcriptase ribozyme can incorporate all four dNTPs.

claim: The reverse transcriptase ribozyme can generate products containing up to 32 deoxynucleotides.

claim: The reverse transcriptase activity could likely be improved through evolution.

claim: The ribosome is present in all extant life.
source: Perhaps the strongest evidence in support of this hypothesis is the ribosome, present in all extant life, which is an RNA enzyme that catalyzes the RNA-instructed synthesis of polypeptides (Nissen et al., 2000).

claim: The ribosome is an RNA enzyme that catalyzes the RNA-instructed synthesis of polypeptides.

claim: Reverse transcriptase catalyzes the RNA-dependent polymerization of DNA.

claim: Reverse transcriptase is responsible for maintaining genetic information in the more stable form of DNA.
